slides.0.title: Côtes de Provence and Its Five Denominations
slides.0.subtitle: The largest AOC, with Sainte-Victoire, Fréjus, La Londe, Pierrefeu and Notre-Dame des Anges
slides.1.title: The largest AOC
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Scale
slides.1.highlights.0.content: CIVP 2025: Côtes de Provence produced 902,027 hl, of which 814,611 hl was rosé, about nine tenths; the INAO specification lists 84 communes (68 in Var, 15 in Bouches-du-Rhône, 1 in Alpes-Maritimes); sources differ on commune count and area ("over 85", "over 20,000 ha"), so these are not tested
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Variety rules
slides.1.highlights.1.content: INAO (2023 revision): principal varieties for red and rosé must total at least 70%, with at least two and none above 90%; some sources say 80%, which differs from INAO, so INAO is followed. Base AOC yield is 55 hl/ha (ceiling 66)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Three colours
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The base AOC covers white, red and rosé; white's principal varieties are Clairette, Sémillon, Ugni Blanc and Vermentino
slides.1.content: Rosé is the core of this AOC.
slides.2.title: Five complementary denominations
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Sainte-Victoire and Fréjus
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Both cover red and rosé only; Sainte-Victoire's principals are Cinsault, Grenache and Syrah, with Grenache and Syrah together at least 50%; Fréjus rosé needs at least 20% Tibouren (INAO); both denominations date from 2005 (Wikipedia)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: La Londe
slides.2.highlights.1.content: The only denomination that also makes white: its principal variety is Vermentino at least 50%; established in 2008 (INAO, Wikipedia)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Pierrefeu and Notre-Dame des Anges
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Pierrefeu (2013) caps red at 45 hl/ha and rosé at 50; Notre-Dame des Anges (2019) has Cinsault, Grenache and Syrah as principals with Carignan up to 10% (INAO, Wikipedia)
slides.2.content: A denomination is a stricter tier within the AOC, not a separate AOC.
slides.3.title: Where denominations are stricter
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Yield
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Base AOC 55 hl/ha; Sainte-Victoire, Fréjus, La Londe and Notre-Dame des Anges 50 hl/ha, Pierrefeu red 45; denomination yields are at least 5 hl/ha below the AOC (INAO)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Ripeness and alcohol
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Minimum natural alcohol for denominations: rosé 11.5%, red 12%; the base AOC needs 11% (INAO)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Load per hectare
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Maximum average load per hectare: 9,500 kg for the AOC and 8,500 kg for denominations, falling to 7,000 and 6,500 kg on irrigated plots (INAO)
slides.3.content: Denomination = lower yields, higher ripeness, tighter variety rules.
